title: Build a collaborative, auditable budget in a week
summary: The latest company, product, and CFO news from Cashboard.
body_markdown:
### *Meet Cashboard, a new way for finance teams to build and manage budgets collaboratively, powered by the AI tools your team already uses.*


“Hey, checking in on that template – is that ready yet?”


Every FP&A person sends this message countless times during budget season.


When I was a CFO, budget owners ignored me half the time, and sent me mangled spreadsheets the other half.


The problem isn’t lack of interest; budget owners care a lot about earning the right to spend money.


The real problem is there’s no way to instantly collect submissions from budget owners in natural language, and merge those submissions into the master plan, and have every change explained in an audit trail, all in the format finance needs.


Collaboration in budgeting is a broken process. That’s why people dread hearing from finance during planning season.


And by the time the numbers finally come together, the budget is already out of date. Priorities shift, actuals get rolled forward, and the business drifts away from the plan. But re-forecasting requires more lengthy, brutal data trudging.


So companies grit their teeth, work from numbers that no longer reflect reality, and wonder what the point of budgeting was in the first place.


We think there’s a better way.


**Meet Cashboard.**


Cashboard is an AI-native collaborative budgeting platform that brings finance and every budget owner into one shared, fully auditable plan.


It’s built for finance teams that already use AI across their business and need a better way to collect inputs, track changes, and manage a bottoms-up planning process. Everyone can work in the AI tools they already know, while giving finance the visibility and control to keep the process moving.


Cashboard helps FP&A teams build a board-ready budget in a fraction of the time compared to legacy budgeting tools. And because it makes budgeting faster and easier than ever, you can re-forecast effortlessly whenever you want.


## A budget everyone can contribute to, without the spreadsheet chaos


Imagine starting with last year’s budget model, updating the drivers and pulling in fresh actuals from your existing systems, and having a detailed plan ready for review *in minutes* . Then imagine getting input from every department without emailing a single spreadsheet attachment or scheduling a meeting called “FY27 Budget Review – Marketing (Round 7).”


That’s the idea behind Cashboard.


Cashboard works through the AI platforms your team already uses, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot. There’s no lengthy implementation, engineering project, or entirely new system for everyone to learn. Simply connect Cashboard to your AI platform (such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini), tell it what you want to plan, and you’re off.


In a matter of days, you’ll have a fully auditable budget ready to go. Here’s what getting started with Cashboard looks like in practice:


### Start with a prompt (spreadsheets optional).


Every budget starts somewhere, usually with last year’s model.


With Cashboard, it starts with a chat. Tell your AI assistant what you want to build with Cashboard; you don’t have to start from scratch. Attach last year’s budget for context, customize the structure, or ask for something entirely new.


Cashboard connects to the systems you’ve already made available to your AI tool of choice, so your AI tool can pull your actuals into your plan. You can also import CSV files and review new information before it’s merged into your budget.


Within minutes, Cashboard creates a detailed budget structure, fills it with granular data, and builds out the drivers and calculations behind every line item. It even creates individual, pre-populated worksheets for each budget owner, so finance doesn’t have to spend days building templates before anyone else can get involved.


### Cashboard shows receipts for every number in the plan.


One of the biggest challenges with using AI for financial planning is knowing where the numbers came from and whether you can trust them. If you can’t explain to the board how a number got into the budget, you’re going to have a bad time.


Cashboard makes every calculated cell traceable. Each calculation uses familiar Excel syntax, and you can click into any cell to see its underlying formula, source records, and assumptions.


Cashboard also comes with a full audit trail that records every change made to the plan. Finance never has to root through scattered templates to trace back version histories, or ping budget owners to ask where something came from.


So when someone asks why software expenses are projected to increase, you don’t have to go digging through a collection of spreadsheets and Slack threads for an answer. Cashboard shows its math and exactly where each number came from.


### Get input from everyone without becoming the budget police.


Finance has built the model. Now it’s time to get everyone else involved.


-


Marketing needs to submit campaign spend.


-


Sales needs to forecast pipeline.


-


CS needs to weigh in on churn.


-


HR needs to update hiring assumptions.


Everyone is expected to make contributions in the right spreadsheet, using the right format, by the right deadline (which always slips, we know).


Cashboard takes this tedious coordination and spreadsheet management off finance’s plate. It collects input from each budget owner about their part of the plan through an interview-style chat. No complicated template to fill out, no spreadsheet fluency required.


Owners answer questions, provide context, and request changes in plain English. For example, a marketing leader could ask Cashboard to pull projected Q3 campaign spend from their team’s spreadsheets, or a sales leader could have it review Slack conversations to help forecast next year’s pipeline. Cashboard gathers the information, pulls data from relevant systems, and updates the appropriate worksheets.


Cashboard also maintains permissions and versions across every AI tool and the Cashboard web app, so budget owners can collaborate where they are most comfortable. Once owners submit their contributions, finance can review everything in one place. Changes are highlighted, the activity feed records who made each edit and when, and finance can approve a submission or send it back for revisions with a single click.


Everyone works from the same plan, and finance stays in control. No templates needed.


### And when the business changes? Your budget can, too.


Businesses don’t operate on a predictable, annual schedule. New hires get approved, projects get delayed, marketing reallocates spend, and revenue comes in differently than expected. Yet many companies are still working from a plan assembled months earlier because updating it feels too time-consuming or expensive.


With Cashboard, monthly re-forecasting is effortless.


Roll forward your forecast with new actuals, model different scenarios, or let budget owners update their assumptions. Cashboard updates the plan and flags what’s changed, so you can focus on reviewing the differences instead of auditing everything all over again.


### Yes, you can still use Excel.


Finance teams love Excel, and we do too! It’s familiar, flexible, and has been doing the heavy lifting of financial planning for decades. Cashboard was designed to work with it.


Export your entire plan into a workbook, complete with a P&L overview and individual tabs for every worksheet. Live formulas and links between tabs mean the file works the exact same way it does in Cashboard.


And if you want to make adjustments to how the model works in Excel, go for it. You can bring those changes back into Cashboard with a simple prompt through your AI assistant, review the updates, and decide when they should be applied to the shared plan.


## Claude + Excel can build a plan – but Cashboard can manage the process, end to end.


You can absolutely ask Claude to build a model in Excel in an afternoon. But mapping out a spreadsheet and providing the purpose-built infrastructure to make collaborative budgeting manageable, accurate, and traceable are two different things.


The hard part about budgeting isn’t the modeling. It’s getting input from 15 different people, ensuring accuracy across everyone’s numbers, tracking your full change history, and knowing where every assumption came from. Cashboard equips teams with the full package: a shared plan, individual ownership, traceable calculations, permissions, and change history to manage all of that in one place.


And compared to legacy tools that might check all these boxes, Cashboard is easy to say yes to. Every contract with Cashboard is month-to-month with a same-day implementation time, unlike legacy tools that require months-long implementations and multi-year contracts before you even know whether the tool works for your team.


## Finance stays in the driver’s seat


Making budgeting easier doesn’t mean giving up control. Finance decides who owns, sees, and edits each part of the plan. Every change is recorded, versions are saved, and submissions can be reviewed and approved before they become part of the budget. Cashboard also undergoes SOC 2 Type II audits and supports single sign-on (SSO).


The point isn’t to replace finance’s judgment with AI. It’s to get rid of the repetitive work—chasing templates, manually merging submissions, spreadsheet maintenance, and version control—so teams have more time for the conversations and tradeoffs that lead to better business decisions.


Cashboard was built by people who know that process firsthand. Our founder and CEO, Julian Rowlands, was the first CFO of Xendit and later led finance at Spruce. Today, he talks with finance leaders about how they’re using AI through[CFOs on AI](https://cfosonai.cashboard.co/) , our Substack interview series. Those conversations are shaping Cashboard into a product built around the real needs of AI-first finance teams.


## Be the hero who turns budget season into budget week


Most finance teams get started with Cashboard in about seven minutes. No implementation project, no engineering dependency, and no long-term commitment: every contract is month-to-month, so there’s no risk in trying it.
